definitions.explanation: The act of combining separate elements into a unified whole; merging organizations, systems, or ideas.

examples.japanese: システムを{統合|とうごう}する。
{二|ふた}つの{会社|かいしゃ}が{統合|とうごう}された。
ヨーロッパ{統合|とうごう}は{長|なが}い{歴史|れきし}がある。
examples.english: European integration has a long history.

notes:
{統合|とうごう} means combining separate elements into a unified whole. Used broadly across business, IT, politics, and organizational contexts.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を: システムを{統合|とうごう}する
- Passive common: {統合|とうごう}される (to be integrated/merged)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経営|けいえい}{統合|とうごう}: business integration, merger
- システム{統合|とうごう}: system integration
- {統合|とうごう}{失調症|しっちょうしょう}: schizophrenia (medical term)
- {地域|ちいき}{統合|とうごう}: regional integration

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {合併|がっぺい}: merger (specifically of companies or municipalities)
- {連携|れんけい}: cooperation, coordination (looser than {統合|とうごう})
- {一元化|いちげんか}: centralization (bringing under one authority)
- {統一|とういつ}: unification (often political or standardization)
